facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with new and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy
Two years earlier, he had undergone a wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
An incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved, with no evidence of distant metastatic disease
no evidence of distant metastatic disease
Multiple satellite lesions were present on the left posterior auricular scalp area
clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation were noted
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
CD163 and myeloperoxidase: Highlighted histiocytes and neutrophils respectively
complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation; MART-1 immunostain confirms complete tumor regression
he received 4 cycles of ipilimumab, followed by a second wide local excision when new lesions appeared
after 5 cycles, local progression occurred in the satellite lesions
